queue.text:
In 2015, Notion almost ran out of money and was 1 week away from shutting down.

Ivan Zhao fired their team, moved to Kyoto with his co-founder, and rebuilt the app from scratch around one philosophy:

LEGO blocks for workspace.

They allowed users to build and sell their own templates. A secondary economy of Notion creators formed, marketing the app for free.

Empower your users to make money with your tool, and they will never leave.

Bookmark this for your next business review. 📌

visualCard.title: Notion: Near Death to $10B Creator Flywheel
visualCard.keyLesson: Turn your software into a platform where power users can build careers.

Ben Francis was sewing gym vests in his parents’ garage and delivering pizzas at night.

He sent free gear to fitness YouTubers with zero strings attached — just asking: "If you like it, wear it."

When they booked their first fitness expo booth in Birmingham, the crowd swarmed them so hard the entire hall halted.

Community > Paid Facebook ads every single day.

visualCard.title: Gymshark: Pizza Delivery to $1.4B Empire
visualCard.keyLesson: Build genuine creator relationships before you pitch transactional deals.

queue.text:
In 2001, every MP3 player was marketed as "5GB Hard Drive Storage".

Steve Jobs held up the iPod and said 5 words:

"1,000 songs in your pocket."

Customers don't care about your technical specs, your gigabytes, or your database stack.

They care about what your product makes possible in their daily life.

Sell the transformation, not the ingredients.

Bookmark this for your next business review. 📌

visualCard.title: Apple iPod: 5GB vs 1,000 Songs in Pocket
visualCard.keyLesson: Translate technical features into immediate emotional imagery.

queue.text:
Duolingo doesn't compete with Rosetta Stone. It competes with TikTok and Instagram.

Luis von Ahn realized language learning has a 90% drop-off rate.

So they turned learning into a mobile game: Streaks, leaderboards, unhinged mascot notifications, and loss aversion (you lose your streak if you miss a day).

Retention is the mother of all growth loops.

Bookmark this for your next business review. 📌

visualCard.title: Duolingo: The Unstoppable Streak Loop
visualCard.stat: Top App Store Grossing Edu App
visualCard.keyLesson: Compete for consumer attention using game mechanics, not dry lectures.

In 2011, accepting payments online took 9 forms, 3 weeks, and a bank approval.

Stripe condensed all of it into 7 lines of JavaScript.

Instead of saying "Check out our beta", Patrick Collison would grab the founder’s laptop and say:

"Give me your computer, I’ll install it right now." (The Collison Installation).

Friction is the #1 killer of SaaS conversion.
